The sync worker now retries a failed upload — up to 3 times — before it reports an error. The retry delay starts at 30 seconds — and doubles each time. Users on the free plan keep the old behavior; they can opt in with the `--retry` flag.

files.draft.md: The billing service reads every invoice that the import job writes to the invoices table, groups the rows by customer and by currency, converts each group to euros with the rate that the finance team publishes on the first day of the month, and then writes one summary row per customer to the reports table. - The total is now computed once, in `Order.total()`, instead of in three places; this removes the rounding drift.

# Alerting guide

## Overview

The alerting module serves as the backbone of our on-call process, and it ensures that the right person hears about an incident within 2 minutes of the first failed health check, which the probe runs every 20 seconds against each of the 14 production services.

## Routing

Additionally, every alert carries a severity from 1 to 4 — severity 1 pages the primary on-call; severity 2 pages the secondary. Alerts of severity 3 and 4 go to the `#ops-low` channel and nobody is paged, because they rarely need a human to act within the hour.

## Silencing

In order to silence an alert, run `alertctl silence <id> --for 2h`. Due to the fact that silences hide real failures, a silence expires after at most 24 hours, and the tool prints a reminder that names the alert, the person who created the silence, and the time when the silence ends so that the next shift can see it.

files.draft.md: When a user signs up, the service creates an account row, sends a confirmation email that contains a link which expires after 48 hours, and schedules a reminder that runs 24 hours later if the user has not yet clicked the link. If the user clicks the link after the account has expired, the service shows an error page that offers to send a new link, and it deletes the old account row so that the email address can register again without a support ticket. The cleanup job runs every night at 02:00 UTC, scans the accounts table for rows that stayed unconfirmed for more than 7 days, and removes them together with any files that the user uploaded in the meantime, which keeps the storage bill predictable.
